title: Bicyclist Hand Signals (Left Arm Straight Left; Left Arm Up OR Right Arm Straight Right; Left Arm Down to Stop)

no_head_on_same_lane.note: Only one cyclist per panel riding forward; no opposing vehicles in same lane.

no_rhd_cabin.note: No car interiors or steering wheels visible; only rear view of cyclist.

single_bulb_signal.note: Each panel shows one signal with single lit lens: left red, center green, right yellow; other lenses dark.

us_right_hand_traffic.note: All three panels show cyclist on right side with double-yellow centerline on left and white edge line / curb on right.

zero_text.note: No letters, numbers, or words visible on signals, road, clothing, or background; all shapes blank.

scene_match.note: Matches 3-panel brief: left arm horizontal left, right arm horizontal right, left arm down for stop.

result.summary: Three-panel cyclist hand-signal illustration meets all visual rules and correctly teaches left, right, and stop signals.

teaching_correct.note: Hand positions correctly demonstrate left turn, right turn with right arm, and slow/stop with left arm down.

result.what_i_see: Three side-by-side rear views of a helmeted cyclist in pink riding on the right side of a road, showing left arm extended left, right arm extended right, and left arm extended down, each beneath a traffic light.
